edits.match: The fistula operation is done under local anaesthetic and takes about an hour; a fistula is preferred because catheters carry a much higher rate of bloodstream infection
edits.replacement: A fistula is preferred because catheters carry a higher rate of bloodstream infection
edits.reason: UNSUPPORTED: operation duration figure not in the NHS excerpt or the pre-patch record; 'much higher' softened to the supported direction of effect.
SCHEMA: kidney.org is not among the approved reference hosts (nhs.uk / NIH / MedlinePlus / FDA / StatPearls / OpenStax) and does not appear anywhere in the pre-patch corpus.

notes: NHS excerpts support: 3 sessions/week of about 4 hours, hospital or home, tiredness/nausea/cramps/dizziness/low blood pressure, sepsis risk, fluid restriction, CAPD vs APD, peritonitis signs and antibiotic treatment with switch to haemodialysis if severe or recurrent, fewer diet/fluid restrictions on PD. Fistula maturation 6-12 weeks, 2-week PD catheter lead time, 2 L exchanges 4x/day and peritonitis frequency all predate the patch. 30-40 minute exchange time matches NHS wording (general knowledge). 'Survival similar on both types' is mainstream (general knowledge). No protected field changed.
